question.text: How many of Europe's top 20 grocery retailers will have public shrimp welfare commitments before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of the following retailers that, before July 1, 2027, have announced and not retracted any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as the Shrimp Welfare Project's [Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps):

* Ahold Delhaize
* Aldi
* Asda
* Auchan
* Carrefour
* Co-op
* E. Leclerc
* Edeka-Gruppe
* Intermarché
* J. Sainsbury's
* Jerónimo Martins
* Magnit
* Mercadona
* Metro AG
* Migros
* Rewe Group
* Schwarz Group
* Systeme U
* Tesco
* X5 Retail Group
question.fine_print:
A welfare commitment must have been announced at any point before July 1, 2027, including before this question opens, but need not have been implemented.   

In case of grocery retailer mergers, entities are still treated distinctly for purposes of this question. Thus, if two companies in the above list merge and the successor entity has a qualifying policy, then both slots count toward the 10 that are needed for a **Yes** resolution.

research:
## Shrimp welfare commitments among Europe's top 20 grocery retailers: research notes as of 2026-11-19

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-02-16 (last update shown): SWP's "Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?" page names only **6** of the 20 listed retailers as having both electrical stunning and eyestalk ablation-free commitments: Albert Heijn (Ahold Delhaize), Asda, Co-op, Sainsbury's, Tesco and Les Mousquetaires (Intermarché). The other 14, including Aldi, Lidl/Schwarz, Rewe, Carrefour, Auchan, Système U and Leclerc, are not named. The page lists no commitment dates. There is no data file behind it. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)
- The criteria accept "any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments" from credible sources, not only the SWP list. Newer commitments reported elsewhere should therefore count.

### 2. Current status
By my count from credible sources, **12 of 20** already appear to qualify:
- Ahold Delhaize, Asda, Co-op, Sainsbury's, Tesco, Intermarché: all on the SWP list.
- 2026-03-16: Lidl GB (Schwarz Group) removed eyestalk ablation from its core own-brand farmed prawns from January 2026 and will introduce electrical stunning by the end of 2026. This covers Great Britain only. [Responsible Seafood Advocate](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/lidl-gb-bans-eyestalk-ablation-for-farmed-prawns-joining-nine-other-u-k-retailers/)
- 2026-04-09: Aldi Süd announced a global policy: no eyestalk ablation by 2030, electrical stunning by 2035. Trade press reports Aldi Nord targeting 2029 for whiteleg shrimp ablation. [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/04/09/aldi-sud-joins-other-major-uk-supermarkets-with-shrimp-stunning-commitment/), [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/with-aldi-s-d-commitment-all-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-time-bound-shrimp-welfare-standards), [LebensmittelPraxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-aktuell/46138-garnelenzucht-aldi-sued-kontert-kritik-der-tierschuetzer.html)
- Rewe Group guideline: 100% of ASC-certified whiteleg shrimp without eyestalk ablation by 2030, black tiger by 2031. Rewe is in the Responsible Stunning Coalition and plans annual reporting on stunning from 2028. The date of the guideline is unclear; I saw this content only through search snippets because the page returned a 403 error. [Rewe](https://www.rewe-group.com/en/press-and-media/publications/guidelines/guideline-on-fish-and-seafood/)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir reports these French commitments [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/):
  - **Carrefour:** end of eyestalk ablation by 2029, no stunning commitment.
  - **Auchan:** ablation dropped since January 2026, electrical stunning by 2030.
  - **Système U:** ablation banned by end of 2027, stunning by 2030.
  - **Lidl France:** ablation dropped in 2026.
  - **Aldi:** ablation ban in 2031, stunning in 2035.
  - **Leclerc:** no commitment.
- No commitment found for 8 retailers: **E. Leclerc** (confirmed none), **Edeka, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, Mercadona, Metro AG, Migros, X5.** Targeted searches for Edeka, Migros, Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins and Metro turned up nothing on shrimp welfare. I did not search Magnit or X5.

Ambiguities the resolver will have to settle:
- Is the SWP list alone authoritative? It would give 6.
- Does a commitment covering only part of a group count, such as Lidl GB/France or Aldi Süd vs Aldi Nord?
- Does an ablation-only commitment like Carrefour's count?
- Which "Co-op" is meant? Presumably the UK Co-op.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir compares French retailers' commitments (details above). [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-10-16/20: ICAW's French report "Souffrance en rayon" (data as of 2026-10-01) ranks retailers:
  - Both practices covered: Les Mousquetaires, Coopérative U, Auchan, Aldi.
  - Ablation only: Carrefour, Casino, Lidl, Biocoop.
  - No commitment: Leclerc, Picard, Grand Frais.
  
  [Animal Welfare Observatory](https://animalwelfareobservatory.org/actualidad/noticias/icaw-langostinos.html), [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234362)
- 2026-04: Aldi Süd's pledge means all 11 major UK supermarkets now have time-bound targets. [Aquaculture Magazine](https://aquaculturemag.com/2026/04/17/aldi-sud-is-the-latest-of-the-uks-11-leading-supermarket-chains-to-commit-to-shrimp-welfare-goals/)
- 2026-03: Lidl GB commitment. 2026-02: Asda commitment (no ablation by 2027, electrical stunning by 2028). [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/with-aldi-s-d-commitment-all-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-time-bound-shrimp-welfare-standards)

### 4. Base rates
- Rough timeline for the 20 listed retailers: about 2023-24 Albert Heijn and Tesco; 2024-25 Sainsbury's, Co-op and Les Mousquetaires (BBFAW report, September 2025); 2026 Asda, Lidl, Aldi, Auchan, U, Carrefour, and Rewe (date uncertain).
- That is roughly 6 by early 2026 and about 12 by November 2026, so around 6 new retailers in the past 9 to 10 months. Activity has come in campaign waves: UK first, then Germany, then France.
- No seasonal pattern applies.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Metaculus community forecast value and no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question. None of the markets you supplied (beef prices, NYC grocery stores, ECB and others) are relevant.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- ICAW and Mercy for Animals campaigns are ongoing, explicitly targeting Leclerc in France and German retailers, which makes Edeka a likely next target.
- The Responsible Stunning Coalition and Aldi-funded stunning study ends in 2028, so it falls after resolution. Retailers waiting on it may hold off on stunning pledges but could still make ablation pledges.
- Retraction risk: commitments are seldom withdrawn. Lidl GB's end-2026 stunning deadline and Tesco's 2026/27 targets could be missed, but missing a deadline is not the same as retracting.
- SWP may update its list page, which was last updated 2026-02-16.
- I could not verify any upcoming announcements from Mercadona, Metro, Migros, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit or X5.

# Shrimp welfare commitments among Europe's top 20 grocers: research notes (as of 2026-11-19)

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-02-16: The Shrimp Welfare Project page, last updated on this date, lists 12 retailers with both an electrical-stunning commitment and an ablation-free commitment: Tesco, M&S, John Lewis/Waitrose, Ocado, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Morrisons, Iceland, Asda, Albert Heijn, Jumbo and Les Mousquetaires. The page gives no date for each retailer. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)
- Only some of those 12 are on the question's list. Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op and Asda count directly. Intermarché counts through Les Mousquetaires. Ahold Delhaize counts only if its subsidiary Albert Heijn's policy is credited to the group. That makes 5 to 6 on the SWP page alone.
- The SWP page is a simple list on a web page. I found no data file behind it.

## 2. Current status
Under the criteria ("any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments", credible sources accepted), my count from credible sources is about 12 of the 20 already:
- **Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Asda:** listed on the SWP page.
- **Intermarché:** through Les Mousquetaires, listed by SWP.
- **Ahold Delhaize:** through Albert Heijn. I found no policy covering the whole group or Delhaize.
- **Aldi:** Aldi Süd has a global pledge: end eyestalk ablation by 2030-31 and stun electrically by 2035. Aldi Nord plans to phase out ablation by 2029 (whiteleg shrimp) and 2031 (giant tiger prawns). [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/04/09/aldi-sud-joins-other-major-uk-supermarkets-with-shrimp-stunning-commitment/), [Lebensmittelpraxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-aktuell/46138-garnelenzucht-aldi-sued-kontert-kritik-der-tierschuetzer.html)
- **Schwarz Group (Lidl):** Lidl International says ablation has been gone from 100% of its permanent own-label farmed shrimp supply chains since January 2026. It makes no stunning commitment outside the UK. Lidl GB says it will stun electrically by the end of 2026. [Lidl](https://info.lidl/en/our-responsibility/acting-fairly/fish-seafood)
- **Metro AG:** asks all shrimp suppliers to avoid ablation and requires stunning of all crustaceans in its own-label products. It gives no deadline. [The Fish Site, 2025-11-25](https://thefishsite.com/fr/articles/metro-nouvelles-exigences-etourdissement-produits-mer)
- **Carrefour, Auchan, Système U:** an ICAW report covered in October 2026 (details under section 3).

Weaker or not found:
- **Rewe:** only certified-organic and Naturland shrimp are free of eyestalk manipulation, plus membership of the Aquaculture Welfare Standards Initiative (AWSI). There is no policy for the whole range, so it is borderline. [Rewe guideline](https://www.rewe-group.com/en/press-and-media/publications/guidelines/guideline-on-fish-and-seafood/)
- **E. Leclerc:** no commitment, according to ICAW.
- **Edeka, Migros, Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, X5:** I found nothing.

Interpretation risks for the forecaster:
- Does a subsidiary's commitment count for the parent (Albert Heijn for Ahold Delhaize, Lidl for Schwarz)?
- Does an ablation-only commitment, or one with no deadline (Metro), count?
- Will the resolver rely only on the SWP list? If so, the count would be about 5 to 6 unless SWP updates the page.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-19: ICAW's report on France says:
  - Carrefour bans ablation and is working toward stunning own-label shrimp from 2027.
  - Auchan, Système U and Intermarché commit to ending ablation and to electrical stunning by 2030.
  - Lidl and Casino ban ablation.
  - Leclerc has no commitment.
  - About 50% of the French market had partial or no commitments as of 2026-10-01.
  [consoGlobe](https://www.consoglobe.com/crevettes-elevage-souffrance-animale-supermarches-cg)
- 2026-08: Albert Heijn is working with SWP to verify its stunning commitments. [Shrimp Insights](https://www.shrimpinsights.com/advertorial/future-shrimp-welfare-how-retailers-can-validate-electrical-stunning-commitments)
- 2026-06: Lidl International publishes its shrimp standards, including the ablation-free claim. [Lidl](https://info.lidl/en/our-responsibility/acting-fairly/fish-seafood)
- 2026-04-09: Aldi Süd announces its global pledge. All 11 major UK supermarkets now have time-bound commitments. [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/with-aldi-s-d-commitment-all-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-time-bound-shrimp-welfare-standards)
- 2026-02-12: Asda commits to end ablation by 2027 and stun electrically by 2028. [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/02/12/uks-asda-commits-to-ban-shrimp-eyestalk-ablation-ice-slurry-stunning/)
- Earlier 2026: Lidl GB bans ablation, becoming the 10th of the UK's 11 largest supermarkets with time-bound prawn commitments. [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/lidl-gb-bans-eyestalk-ablation-for-farmed-prawns-joining-nine-other-u-k-retailers/)
- 2025-11-25: Metro AG publishes its stunning and ablation requirements (link in section 2).
- None of the news articles supplied with the brief are relevant.

## 4. Base rates
- **Pace:** Tesco's policy in August 2024 was the first among the listed retailers. [ALI](https://www.ali.fish/blog/two-major-companies-publish-comprehensive-crustacean-welfare-policies) Over about 2 years (mid-2024 to late 2026) the count went from roughly 1 to about 12, which is about 5 to 6 new listed retailers a year. Most came between late 2025 and October 2026, so the pace has been speeding up.
- **What is left:** the remaining 8 are mostly in Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Portugal and Russia. These markets have had less campaign pressure, so the past pace may not carry over. Magnit and X5 (Russia) look very unlikely.
- **Retractions:** I found none.
- **Seasonality:** none relevant.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question, or the Metaculus community forecast.
- None of the prediction-market prices supplied with the brief match this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (2027-07-01)
- **Rewe and Edeka:** possible responses to German campaigns. ICAW and influencer campaigns have been targeting German discounters. [Lebensmittelpraxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-aktuell/46847-garnelenzucht-neue-kampagne-gegen-aldi-gestartet.html)
- **Migros:** under pressure from Swiss animal-welfare groups over its welfare claims in general. I found no campaign specific to shrimp.
- **Mercadona:** reportedly handles about a quarter of Spain's farmed shrimp, making it a likely campaign target. [Rethink Priorities](https://rethinkpriorities.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Estimating-The-Number-Of-Shrimp-In-The-Spanish-Retail-Market.pdf)
- **SWP page update:** likely to add Aldi, Lidl, Metro, Carrefour, Auchan and Système U.
- **Deadlines falling before resolution:** Tesco's 2026 targets, Lidl GB stunning by the end of 2026, and Carrefour stunning from 2027. Missing a deadline is not the same as retracting a commitment.
- **ASC "Responsible Shrimp Slaughter" project:** results are due in 2028, which is after resolution.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 7.4 months, until 1 July 2027. The question resolves around 1 July 2027.

(b) **Latest known value:**
- The SWP list (updated 2026-02-16) names 6 of the 20 retailers.
- Counting other credible sources, 12 qualify as of November 2026. On top of the 6, these are Schwarz/Lidl, Aldi, Rewe, Carrefour, Auchan and Système U.

(c) **If nothing changes:** about 12 under a lenient reading of "any commitment, credible sources", or 6 if the resolver uses only the SWP list.

(d) **If the trend continues:** about 6 new retailers committed in roughly 9 months. The remaining pool is harder, though: Leclerc, Edeka, Mercadona, Migros, Metro, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit and X5. Magnit and X5 are very unlikely. A plausible 1 to 3 more gives 13 to 15.

(e) **Historical variation:** commitments have come in campaign waves, UK first, then Germany, then France. Over a 7-month window, gains of 0 to 4 seem realistic.

(f) **Experts and markets:** there are no markets on this. Campaigners (ICAW, Mercy for Animals) are actively targeting Leclerc and the German retailers, which suggests Edeka is a likely next target.

(g) **Scenarios:**
- **Low:** the resolver relies strictly on the SWP list, or rejects partial-group (Lidl GB/France) and ablation-only (Carrefour) commitments, giving 6 to 9.
- **High:** Edeka, Leclerc, Mercadona and Migros all commit under campaign pressure, and Metro adds a policy, giving 16 to 17.
